'''Takei-Otake-no-Mikoto''' (武五百建命, also written as たけいおたけのみこと, たけいおたつのみこと, [[birth and death dates unknown]]) was a [[Kofun period]] [[gōzoku]] (local noble) and the first '''{{ill|Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|科野国造|qid=Q11595951|lt=Shina no Kuni no Miyatsuko}}'''. In the "{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|ja|国造本紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuzō Honki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q133833194}}" section of the {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}}, he is referred to as '''Tatei-Otake-no-Mikoto'''.

== Overview ==

According to the "{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|ja|国造本紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuzō Honki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q133833194}}" section of the {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}}, Takei-Otake-no-Mikoto was the grandson of {{ill|Kamuyaimimi|fr|Kamuyaimimi|ja|神八井耳命|ko|카무야이미미노미코토|simple|Kamuyaimimi|zh|神八井耳命|qid=Q11588756|lt=Kamuyaimimi}} and was appointed as the first '''{{ill|Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|科野国造|qid=Q11595951|lt=Shina no Kuni no Miyatsuko}}''' during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}. Tradition holds that he founded the {{ill|Shinano Ōmiyasha|ja|科野大宮社}}.

== Genealogy ==

Takei-Otake-no-Mikoto is said to be the grandson of {{ill|Kamuyaimimi|fr|Kamuyaimimi|ja|神八井耳命|ko|카무야이미미노미코토|simple|Kamuyaimimi|zh|神八井耳命|qid=Q11588756|lt=Kamuyaimimi}}<ref>“{{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}},” Kokuzō Honki, Kuno Kokuzō entry.</ref>.

== Shrines Enshrining Him ==

*{{ill|Futago Shrine (Ueda City)|ja|二子神社 (上田市)}} ({{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}, {{ill|Ueda, Nagano|en|Ueda, Nagano|qid=Q844852|lt=Ueda City}})
*{{ill|Susu Kizumi Shrine (Chikuma City)|ja|須須岐水神社 (千曲市)}}, within its grounds, the Iwai Shrine (Nagano Prefecture, {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|en|Chikuma, Nagano|qid=Q179757|lt=Chikuma City}}, Yashiro)
*{{ill|Karasaki Shrine (Chikuma City)|ja|唐崎神社 (千曲市)}} (Nagano Prefecture, Chikuma City, Amamiya)
